context: PDF slow-open user feedback (16:42 BJT), accompanied by user screenshot
scope: Read-only investigation and evidence. No production repair/source edits. Feedback correction held for user approval per PROJECT_RULES.md.

currentFrontend.note: Separately bounded stages do not imply end-to-end 45-second time limit. Authorize + transfer + initial parse may extend toward minutes on a degraded network.

workerChange.feature: Bind private PDF v2 tickets to originating login; check session token hash on each Range request to honor device revocation.
workerChange.dbLookup: SELECT token_hash FROM user_sessions WHERE token_hash=? AND user_id=? AND expires_at>?
workerChange.confirmedRegression: One extra indexed D1 check per ticketed Range request; latency impact on owner Mainland Edge not measured.
workerChange.securityConstraint: Do not disable immediate logout / device-revocation check without approved safety design.

publicProbe.limitation: Synthetic invalid bearer only. No authorized owner open, R2 file download, real browser network, mobile ISP, university VPN or PDF.js paint latency tested in production.

openHypotheses: Campus/China to Cloudflare RTT or file throughput is degraded.
First-page PDF.js parsing waits for several non-linearized distant R2 ranges.
Additional indexed D1 lookup may add some per-range latency but no minutes-long regression proven.
Concurrent publisher/media capture could share Worker/D1/R2 resources, but no direct load measurements confirm impact.
nextSuggestedApprovedInterventions: Display sanitized phase-level progress and timed metrics while the PDF is still loading, not only after an error.
Use a bounded first-page strategy and avoid duplicative fallback work, preserving authorization and Range correctness.
Complete Tencent independent TLS and owner authenticated 206 acceptance before enabling a zero-cost fallback.
Keep explicit local-saving path for repeated PDFs to avoid recurring network downloads; do not silently upload or share PDFs.
